verdict.rationale: Google Cloud documents the scriptable `gcloud` CLI (authentication, configuration, developer workflow) and Cloud APIs for automating workflows via REST or client libraries. It also documents Terraform-based declarative infrastructure and Workload Identity Federation, which gives external workloads access without service account keys. Together these are strong building blocks for headless and CI use, but no evidence item explicitly documents non-interactive or CI-pipeline operation. missing for 10: explicit documentation of headless/non-interactive gcloud usage in CI pipelines (e.g., CI provider integration or a non-interactive auth walkthrough), independent hands-on corroboration of CI automation

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: The `gcloud` CLI manages authentication, local configuration, developer workflow, and interactions with the Google Cloud APIs.
Google Cloud APIs allow you to automate your workflows by using your favorite language.
Using Workload Identity Federation, you can provide on-premises or multicloud workloads with access to Google Cloud resources by using federated identities instead of a service account key.
Define your infrastructure declaratively using Terraform.
